root_cause_label: Pip installed packages to /usr/local/lib/python3.13 but python3 ran from openhands venv; agent pivoted to installing torch instead of fixing interpreter path
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent installed datasets/transformers into the system Python prefix but executed the script via the openhands venv interpreter which lacked those packages, then exhausted the step budget by pursuing an unnecessary torch/CUDA installation instead of fixing the interpreter path mismatch.
t_err_evidence: Step 1: Agent ran bare 'pip install datasets transformers' without verifying which Python interpreter pip targets; packages landed in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages, not in the openhands venv that the 'python3' command resolves to.
t_commit_evidence: Step 6: Agent pivoted to installing torch and CUDA libraries (totally unnecessary for token counting), consuming all remaining steps in giant downloads and never returning to fix the interpreter path issue.
t_surface_evidence: Step 3: 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named datasets' when running python3 /app/calculate_tokens.py, demonstrating that the venv python3 cannot find the packages installed in /usr/local.
trigger_explanation: At step 1, the agent assumed that running 'pip install' would make packages available to whichever 'python3' is invoked by default in the environment, without verifying whether pip and python3 share the same prefix. In fact pip targeted /usr/local while python3 resolved to /opt/openhands-venv/bin/python3.
forewarning_evidence: Step 4 re-runs the same 'pip install datasets transformers' and the output reveals the split: datasets is listed as already satisfied in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages while many other requirements are satisfied in /opt/openhands-venv. This clearly shows two distinct Python environments, signaling the root cause before the agent committed to the wrong fix.
